document.abstract: An ion exchange system has been developed to purify photographic wash water and allow its re-use. The effluent from a print-washing machine is cycled through a cation and then an anion exchange resin bed, and returned to the machine. The purity of the water obtained approaches that of distilled water. This unit was developed for the United States Signal Corps, to be used in mobile photographic units, and is designed to reduce the amount of water required for print-washing. This process is applicable not only to circumstances where water is scarce, but also to processes where wash-water purity and temperature control are important, as in color photography.
